newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, expected to firm.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, expected to firm.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on higher volume and turnover on Wednesday, and analysts expected them to firm further amid strong buying interest.
"Most stocks rise by 2.0-3.0 percent every day and I think this trend of mild growth will continue," said Igor Kos of the Taurus brokerage.
Five of 12 active issues rose, five fell, one was flat and one traded for the first time. Volume was up at 17,121 shares, turnover doubled to 10.5 million kuna.

Kos said food processor Podravka was a hot stock at the Zagreb Stock Exchange at the moment. It was the most active issue on Wednesday, edging up 16 kuna to reach its nominal value of 300 kuna on volume of 10,956 units.
"People are looking for a new stock to buy. Zagrebacka Banka and (drugs firm) Pliva are too expensive now for some investors to buy big packages," he said.
Zagrebacka Banka rose 27.10 kuna to 1,650.10 kuna after peaking at 1,700. It sold 3,892 shares.
Kos said Zagrebacka could score new gains, but on smaller volume as its share offer was scarce. Its GDRs fetched $30 on Seaq, up from $29.375 on Tuesday.
Zagrebacka's preference E-series stock fell 30 kuna to 950, selling 227 shares.
Pliva added 10 kuna to 510, selling 385 shares. Its GDRs traded at $17.0/17.125 in London.
Top gainer hotelier Arenaturist rose 10 kuna to 170, with 58 shares sold.

Another hotelier, Jadranturist, was the top loser, dipping 18 kuna to 280 with 795 shares sold. Laguna and Istraturist were also on the losing side, both down 10 kuna to 1,240 and 190 kuna, respectively.

Adriatic pipeline Janaf made its debut at the Zagreb bourse on Wednesday, closing at 5,500 kuna, up from its 1,000 kuna nominal value. Market participants predicted livelier trading with the pipeline in the future, particularly ahead of its flotation.
Chocolate maker Kras lost 26 kuna to 453, with 492 units changing hands.
